GERMAN — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #7
====

GRADE: Grade 5
SUBJECT: GERMAN
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. “Guten Tag” means: (1 mark)
   A. Thank you
   B. Good day / hello
   C. Good night
   D. Please

2. When practising Reading Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Reading Comprehension.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading Comprehension.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading Comprehension.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Reading Comprehension.

3. When practising Reading Aloud, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading Aloud.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading Aloud.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading Aloud.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading Aloud.

4. When practising Listening for gist, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for gist.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for gist.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Listening for gist.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Listening for gist.

5. When practising Phonological awareness , Imitative speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Phonological awareness , Imitative speaking.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Phonological awareness , Imitative speaking.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Phonological awareness , Imitative speaking.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonological awareness , Imitative speaking.

6. German for “school” is: (1 mark)
   A. Haus
   B. Wasser
   C. Schule
   D. Buch

7. When practising Imitative speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Imitative speaking.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Imitative speaking.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Imitative speaking.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Imitative speaking.

8. When practising Reading aloud, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Reading aloud.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading aloud.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Reading aloud.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading aloud.

9. When practising Guided writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Guided writing.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Guided writing.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Guided writing.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Guided writing.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
10. In three clear sentences, explain Listening for gist and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

11. In three clear sentences, explain Phonological awareness , Imitative speaking and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

12. In three clear sentences, explain Imitative speaking and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

13. In three clear sentences, explain Imitative speaking and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. B — Good day / hello

2. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading Comprehension.

3. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading Aloud.

4. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for gist.

5. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonological awareness , Imitative speaking.

6. C — Schule

7. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Imitative speaking.

8. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading aloud.

9. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Guided writing.

10. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Listening for gist; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

11. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Phonological awareness , Imitative speaking; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

12. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Imitative speaking; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Imitative speaking; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
